uncited: Block-based Data Partitioning is a chunk-based spatial partitioning method that uses 3D rectangular slabs of adjacent cells (blocks) as the atomic unit for data indexing and I/O, rather than individual cells.
It solves the problem of excessive storage overhead in external index structures caused by data duplication at the cell level.
- Output: A partitioned dataset structure where data is organized into blocks, enabling efficient external indexing and progressive isosurface extraction.
The external index structure is built using blocks as the atomic unit.
Each block is a 3D rectangular slab of adjacent cells.
The layout is defined by the block dimensions in voxels/cells.
**Define Block Granularity:** Determine the dimensions of a block.
**Partition Data:** Divide the global volume domain into 3D rectangular slabs of adjacent cells.
**Build External Index:** Construct the external index structure using the blocks as the atomic unit.
**Access Data:** When querying or rendering, load entire blocks.
